title: Quarterly Retail E-Commerce Sales — Q3 2026 (the nonstore quarter the Prime-Day shift runs through), 10:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: census.gov/retail/release_schedule.html, the SAME primary page this calendar already uses for the monthly MARTS entries, fetched direct 2026-09-09 during the retail-sales-2026-09-16 D-7 pulse. Its Quarterly Retail E-Commerce Sales table reads '3rd Quarter 2026 | November 19, 2026', with the page stating all e-commerce reports release at 10:00 am; the four preceding rows on the same table (3rd Quarter 2025 -> December 18, 2025; 4th Quarter 2025 -> March 10, 2026; 1st Quarter 2026 -> May 18, 2026; 2nd Quarter 2026 -> August 18, 2026) give the cadence, and the Q2 2026 row is independently corroborated by the release itself having published on 2026-08-18. Filed estimate, NOT confirmed, on two counts and neither of them is doubt about the date: this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and only ONE primary page was read this session (the advance-services-q3-2026-11-19 precedent in this calendar required two independent census.gov primaries -- the economic-indicators calendar-listview AND the program's own schedule table -- before promoting estimate -> confirmed, and that second read was not performed here). Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Proposed because the calendar tracks the MONTHLY retail series four times over (retail-sales-2026-09-16 / -10-15 / -11-17 / -12-16) and carries no entry at all for the QUARTERLY e-commerce report, which is the only published Census measure that isolates the single line item the proposing ledger's entire arithmetic rests on. That ledger's base case is that August 2026 headline retail sales carry ~+0.65pp of purely mechanical lift, of which ~+0.41pp (headline) / ~+0.76pp (control group) is nonstore normalizing after Amazon moved Prime Day from July to June -- and both of its registered forward tests, FT-retail-sales-2026-09-16-1 and -2, depend on that assumption without measuring it. The Q2 2026 edition (released 2026-08-18, read 2026-09-09) is what makes the series worth tracking rather than merely adjacent: e-commerce printed $340.2B, +3.8% q/q and +12.2% y/y, at 17.1% of ~$2.0T total retail (+2.9% q/q). Nonstore is therefore the fastest-growing line in the report by roughly 7pp against the monthly headline's +5.0% y/y -- which reframes July's -2.2% monthly nonstore print as an anomaly against a strongly positive structural trend rather than as evidence of consumer weakness. The Q3 2026 edition is the one whose reference quarter (July-September) CONTAINS the Prime-Day shift on both sides, so it is the quarterly settlement of the monthly argument. It also separates the proposing ledger's dollars-up/units-flat thesis into its two halves in a way no monthly print can: the monthly nonstore line is seasonally adjusted dollars, while the quarterly report publishes e-commerce as a SHARE of total retail, and a share is unmoved by an inflator that lifts numerator and denominator together. Filed low impact deliberately, following the umich-sentiment-prelim-2026-09-11 and consumer-credit-2026-10-07 precedents set by this same proposing lane: the calendar's header comment carries a standing judgment that second-order consumer reads are omitted, and this is a 10:00 ET quarterly release with no house playbook keyed to it (symbols: [], macro-print), landing two days after its own monthly sibling retail-sales-2026-11-17 has already moved the tape. It widens caution and never licenses an entry. CONSIDERED AND DECLINED alongside it, so their absence reads as a decision rather than an oversight: the Q4 2026 edition, whose date the schedule table does not yet carry; and the Johnson Redbook weekly same-store index, which the proposing ledger has quoted at every pulse since 2026-09-01 (+9.1% -> +9.6% y/y) but which is a weekly private subscription series with no fixed published calendar row, exactly the class this table omits. Note 2026-11-19 already carries advance-services-q3-2026-11-19 (Census's own AIES benchmark release for services) at the same 10:00 ET slot -- Census bundles these, which is corroboration of the slot rather than a conflict. Discovered during the retail-sales-2026-09-16 D-7 pulse (2026-09-09), on the same release_schedule.html fetch that performed that pulse's eighth consecutive re-verification of the 2026-09-16 08:30 ET date.
